text:
[BERT4Rec’s original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690) trains random Cloze targets and additionally describes examples masking only the final item to align training with appended-mask inference. This establishes task alignment, not automatic learning of recency or an epoch schedule. The [authors’ released generator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/master/gen_data.py) builds overlapping chronological windows, anchored backward from the history’s end, and duplicates them with random masks. Its training entry point uses `force_last=False`; `force_last=True` selects the latest window and masks its final real item for evaluation. Thus, this released code does not implement the paper’s explicit terminal-only training mixture, nor sample arbitrary terminal prefixes.

Loss normalization differs between description and implementation. Paper equation 8 averages negative log-likelihood over masked targets within each sequence; averaging these sequence losses would give examples equal weight. The [released trainer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/master/run.py) instead divides summed masked-target losses across the batch by the total valid-target count, excluding padded targets. Examples with more targets consequently receive greater weight. A terminal-example sampling probability therefore need not equal its share of the training loss; per-example normalization or separately normalized objective terms makes that distinction explicit.

[Recency Sampling research](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643) supports explicitly favoring recent targets, with benefits across several architectures, but studies removal of sampled targets and multiple-positive prediction—not BERT4Rec prefix curricula. It provides indirect motivation, not evidence for a particular scheduled terminal-mask mixture. A reproducible experimental curriculum should specify user sampling, prefix-end distribution, context truncation, terminal probability by training step, random-mask rate, and loss normalization; compare against fixed mixtures using validation. Mask the terminal target completely and omit its future suffix. Any proposed schedule remains a hypothesis.
